bib.title: Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks" (method name AdaCoM). Lu Yi*, Runlin Lei* (co-first), Liuyi Yao, Yuexiang Xie, Yuyang Li, Wenhao Zhang, Zhewei Wei†, Yaliang Li†, Jian-Yun Nie. Renmin Univ. of China, Tongyi Lab (Alibaba), BUPT, Université de Montréal. arXiv:2605.30785v1 [cs.AI], 29 May 2026. Preprint. The text has ACL-style Limitations and ethics sections, but no venue is stated. Code is at an anonymous.4open.science link (App. E), not a public repo.

COVERAGE: about 87,213 of 87,213 chars read. That includes the body, limitations, Tables 1-6, and Appendices A-D. Appendices E-G (code, licences, AI-use) were also read. In Appendix H I read the prompt tables 7-9 and the start of the judge prompts (Tables 10-11). The tail of Table 11 and Table 12 (the extraction prompt) were not read; they are judge/extraction prompt boilerplate. References were skimmed. Figures were not rendered. Figure 4 and Figure 5 bar values come from the text extraction.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: A small external manager (Qwen3-4B-Instruct) trained with RL to edit a frozen agent's context beats vanilla ReAct on BrowseComp-Plus for all four agents.
  number: mean@3 average 24.17 -> 33.60, +39.0% relative. Kimi +95.0%.
  setup: BrowseComp-Plus, 680 train / 150 test, 35 max iterations, Qwen3-Embed-8B retriever, GPT-4o judge. Agents are Qwen3-Max, Kimi-K2, GLM-4.5-Air and DeepSeek-V3. A separate manager is trained per agent. Context is capped at 32K under AdaCoM.
  quote: "achieving an average relative gain of 39.0% and a 95.0% relative gain on Kimi."
  where: Sec 4.2, Table 1
- claim: A fixed summarization manager (SumCoM) is inconsistent. It helps weak agents and hurts strong ones, and it is below AdaCoM on average.
  number: SumCoM avg 29.39 (+21.6%) vs AdaCoM 33.60 (+39.0%). SumCoM on GLM 26.44, -18.8% vs ReAct 32.56.
  setup: same as Table 1. SumCoM is a trained Qwen3-4B manager that only summarizes after each step.
  quote: "SumCoM improves some agents but degrades GLM, suggesting that a fixed summarization operation is not sufficiently compatible with varied agent backbones."
  where: Sec 4.2, Table 1
- claim: Agent-side self-management (SumAgent, MemAct) and an untrained manager do not reliably beat ReAct.
  number: Table 1 averages, mean@3: SumAgent 22.06 (-8.7%), MemAct 25.72 (+6.4%), AdaCoM untrained 22.01 (-8.9%). MemAct scores 37.33 on Qwen, just above AdaCoM's 36.67.
  setup: Table 1. SumAgent follows MEM1/IterResearch. MemAct gives the agent a prune tool.
  quote: "AdaCoM w/o training performs inconsistently and is worse than ReAct on average, indicating that the manager must be trained"
  where: Sec 4.2, Table 1
- claim: Learned strategies differ by agent. Stronger agents get later, lighter compression (tiered management). Weaker agents get near-every-round compression (eager distillation). This is the Fidelity-Reliability Trade-off.
  number: mean post-management context about 1.9K tokens (DeepSeek), 3.4K (Kimi), 5.2K (Qwen), 7.0K (GLM). The order matches ReAct baseline order DeepSeek < Kimi < Qwen < GLM.
  setup: BrowseComp-Plus test set, each agent paired with its own manager.
  quote: "about 1.9K tokens for DeepSeek, 3.4K for Kimi, 5.2K for Qwen, and 7.0K for GLM."
  where: Sec 4.4, Fig 3
- claim: Beyond an agent's effective context length, extra raw context hurts. The authors present this as an inference from the learned strategies, not a direct test.
  number: none
  setup: interpretation of the context-length trend above.
  quote: "preserving raw trajectories retains fine-grained evidence, but beyond an agent's effective context length, additional raw content can harm reasoning. Conversely, aggressive compression improves reliability but may discard details."
  where: Sec 4.4
- claim: The manager learns without being told to keep a compact state message right after the task message. It lists requirements, unresolved constraints, evidence, leads, rejected candidates and failed queries. This fixes constraint forgetting, premature give-up and redundant exploration.
  number: 42.6% of Kimi's tool-use steps per task are repetitive under ReAct.
  setup: BrowseComp-Plus test set, based on paired trajectory inspection (qualitative).
  quote: "On the BrowseComp-Plus test set, an average of 42.6% of Kimi's tool-use steps per task are repetitive."
  where: Sec 4.3
- claim: Gains carry over to deep research (MCP-Bench-Wiki).
  number: mean@3 Kimi 55.05 -> 60.01 (+9.0%), DeepSeek 47.51 -> 58.09 (+22.3%), avg +15.2%. Untrained manager avg is -10.1%.
  setup: 150 test tasks, Wikipedia MCP with 9 tools, Claude Opus 4.6 judge, score = 0.4 TF + 0.4 IG + 0.2 PE. Only 2 agents.
  quote: "achieving 9.0% and 22.3% relative gains on Kimi and DeepSeek, respectively"
  where: Sec 4.2, Table 2
- claim: Managers transfer across agents, best between agents of similar capability. Exceptions come from style mismatch.
  number: 23 of 28 cross-agent pairs improve (plus all 4 self pairs). Mean gain is 25.0% over 32 pairs and 22.1% over the 28 cross pairs. Largest cross gain is 79.6% (Kimi, DeepSeek-trained manager).
  setup: 4 trained managers x 8 target agents on BrowseComp-Plus. Held-out agents are GPT-OSS-20B, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Seed-1.6-Flash and GPT-4o-mini. On MCP-Bench-Wiki, both managers improve all 4 targets.
  quote: "23 of 28 cross-agent pairs, plus all 4 self-trained pairs, achieve positive gains, with an average relative improvement of 25.0% across all 32 pairs and 22.1% across the 28 cross-agent pairs alone."
  where: Sec 5, Fig 4
- claim: Style-compatibility failures. DeepSeek prefers concise key findings plus doc IDs. GLM is hurt by aggressive compression, and a 4B manager may not paraphrase losslessly. Gemini mirrors a report-style memory and gives up early.
  number: none
  setup: trajectory inspection, BrowseComp-Plus.
  quote: "Gemini ... tends to mirror the report format in its own response instead of continuing the search, which can cause the agent to give up early without a valid answer."
  where: App C.3
- claim: Process rewards help.
  number: DeepSeek-V3 26.19 -> 24.38, Qwen3-Max 36.67 -> 33.33 when alpha=0.
  setup: BrowseComp-Plus mean@3, two agents.
  quote: "For DeepSeek-V3, mean@3 drops from 26.19% to 24.38%; for Qwen3-Max, it drops from 36.67% to 33.33%."
  where: App C.2, Table 5
- claim: Pass@3 on BrowseComp-Plus shows the same pattern.
  number: avg ReAct 34.67 -> AdaCoM 48.92 (+41.1%). SumCoM 40.33, MemAct 37.33.
  setup: Table 3.
  quote: "Avg.34.67 33.00↓4.8%37.33↑7.7%40.33 ↑16.3%33.45↓3.5%48.92↑41.1%"
  where: App A/C.1, Table 3
- claim: Case study shows the two strategies in practice. GLM: 11 interventions, 10 of them edit only one ~1K-token working note at message index 1. Raw tool results are left alone, with one batched delete and merge at the end. DeepSeek: 18 interventions, with the latest tool result paraphrased or deleted nearly every round. Raw results are kept at most three rounds.
  number: 11 / 10 / ~1K tokens; 18 interventions; 3 rounds
  setup: task 996, BrowseComp-Plus.
  quote: "Raw results are retained only when they contain evidence for unresolved constraints, and even then for at most three rounds before being paraphrased or deleted."
  where: App D

MECHANISM (for the note)
- Frozen agent. Before each agent step the manager emits a JSON list of edits. Each edit has ids, role, justification and new_content. Empty new_content deletes. Non-empty new_content rewrites or merges. An empty list means no change. The justification is stripped before the agent sees the context.
- Training: SFT warm-up, then GRPO with G=8. Reward is the final-answer reward plus rule-based process rewards. Process reward values: token penalty -0.8, redundant-action penalty -0.4 (same tool call twice in a row), format penalty -0.5, gold-doc-found +0.6, key-doc-found +0.3. alpha=0.1, lr 5e-6, KL 0.006, clip 0.2, temperature 1.0. Lower temperatures gave degenerate repetitive outputs.
- Manager context window is 32,768 tokens, so the agent's effective input is capped at 32K (ReAct baselines used native windows of 128K-256K). This is a confound the paper notes only in App A.
- SFT data on MCP-Bench-Wiki was about 73% modify, 20% extract, and 7% delete or no_change combined. Samples were kept only if a modify cut the targeted content by at least 20%.

LIMITS
- Authors concede: only two knowledge-search task families, no code agents, embodied agents or long-form writing. MCP-Bench-Wiki has only 2 agents for the main result. The 4B manager may lose evidence for strong agents, and the small gain on GLM may partly reflect that. No larger managers were trained.
- Authors concede: a manager call at every step adds token cost and latency. They suggest triggering it only every few rounds or near a length threshold, but do not test this.
- Authors concede: edits to earlier context break KV-cache reuse. This is not optimised. Tiered management is suggested as a mitigation, untested.
- Not shown: no cost, latency or token-count comparison. The 32K cap under AdaCoM versus the native 128-256K windows for ReAct is not separated from the effect of the learned edits. The "effective context length" explanation rests on correlation across four agents.
- Not shown: test sets are 150 tasks with mean@3, and no confidence intervals or significance tests are reported. Several quoted relative gains rest on low base scores (17-33%).
- Not shown: only Qwen3-4B-Instruct was tried as manager.
- Dated: models are those of 2025 to early 2026. It is a single-author-group preprint with no peer review stated.

BUILDS ON: ReAct (Yao et al., 2022). MEM1 (Zhou et al., 2025) and IterResearch (Chen et al., 2025a) for the summary-in-loop baseline (SumAgent). ReSum (Wu et al., 2025) for the summarization prompts and the SumCoM baseline. MemAct "Memory as Action" (Zhang et al., 2025) for the prune-tool baseline. GRPO (Shao et al., 2024), Trinity-RFT (Pan et al., 2025). Benchmarks BrowseComp-Plus (Chen et al., 2025b, from BrowseComp, Wei et al., 2025) and MCP-Bench (Wang et al., 2025). Long-context degradation is cited to Liu et al., 2024 (lost-in-the-middle), Shi et al., 2023 and Xiao et al., 2024. The authors treat long-term memory work (Mem0, A-Mem, Memory-R1, G-Memory) as complementary, not as a baseline.

CODE: none worth keeping, though the Table 9 prompt rules are useful.
Output schema (App H, Table 9):
{"modifications":[{"ids":["<msg_id_1>","<msg_id_2>",...],"role":"user"|"assistant","justification":"<reason>","new_content":"<replacement text, or empty string \"\" to remove>"}]}
Prompt rules worth quoting:
- "Always preserve the original task description — without it, the agent loses task context entirely."
- "Keep recent context detailed; compress older context progressively."
- "overly aggressive summarization can cause redundant work."
- "If the agent is repeating itself, ensure the context clearly shows the action was already taken and its outcome."
- "Do not include next-step instructions in new_content."
- "Use "user" to increase agent attention to critical information."

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): AdaCoM overview. The manager emits an edit plan before each agent step, and only the manager is trained.
- Fig 2: per-agent shift in trajectory outcomes (correct, incorrect, early give-up, max-iterations) as AdaCoM minus ReAct.
- Fig 3: post-management context length per agent. (a) is the distribution, (b) is the per-step trace on task 199. It shows the tiered and eager-distillation shapes at a glance.
- Fig 4: 8x5 transfer bars on BrowseComp-Plus.
- Fig 5: transfer on MCP-Bench-Wiki.
I did not run figures.py.

PROBLEMS: No extraction faults beyond garbled math symbols and table-cell concatenation. The PDF contains no embedded instructions. The numbers in Fig 4 and Fig 5 were read from the extraction and not checked against the images. The Table 1 "Kimi" ReAct baseline is 18.56, and the quoted "79.6%" cross-agent figure is only in the text. The note file grep found no existing citation of this paper in 05-compression-compaction.md (so it is new to that note).
